texts.preamble: T. Suresh, vs State Of A.P., on 28 September, 2022 Author: Juvvadi Sridevi Bench: Juvvadi Sridevi The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Criminal Revision Case Nos.576 and 580 of 2007 Common Order :
texts.facts: 5. The case of the prosecution, in brief, is that on 17.12.2002 at about 12:40 hours, the complainant/Food Inspector, Nalgonda (PW.1) inspected Sri Lakshmi Traders, Nereducherla, along with his office attendant. During the said visit, A1-Garine Saidaiah, proprietor of Sri Lakshmi Traders, was present and was transacting business. PW.1 disclosed his identity to A1 in the presence of LW.2- Vijay Kumar, inspected the premises of Sri Lakshmi Traders and found 40 kilograms of Redgram Dal in an open gunny bag of 50 kilograms capacity, without label. On enquiry by PW.1, A1 stated that the said Redgram Dal was kept for sale to public for human consumption and he purchased the same from M/s. Vishnu Gopal Rajesh Kumar Grain Merchants & Commission Agents T. Suresh, vs State Of A.P., on 28 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156749863/ 1 (A2) under purchase bill No.6936, dated 05.12.2002 . On suspicion, PW.1 purchased 750 grams of Redgram Dal from the stock for Rs.18.75 ps under a cash receipt, served Form No.6 notice to A1 informing his 3 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 intention to send the said Redgram Dal to Public Analyst for analysis and obtained acknowledgement, divided the purchased Redgram Dal into three equal parts of 250 grams each, placed the same into three separate empty dried and clean plastic jars, affixed label of local Health Authority and conducted panchanama, which was attested by panch witness, PW.2. On 18.12.2002, PW.1 sent one part of sealed sample to Public Analyst and the remaining two parts of sealed sample was deposited with local Health Authority, Nalgonda for safe custody. PW.1 received Public Analyst Report under Ex.P18 with covering letter, dated 24.01.2003, who opined that the sample contains synthetic colour 'Tartrazine' and is, therefore, adulterated. On 31.01.2003, PW.1 addressed a letter bearing No.132/NLG/DII/5632/2002 to the supplier of said Redgram Dal (A2) asking him to furnish ownership/license particulars of the firm. In response, A2 submitted the license particulars and stated that they have purchased the said stock of Redgram Dal from A3-M/s. Vijaya Durga Dhal & General Merchants, Macherla, Guntur District, vide bill No.3/9, dated 05.11.2002, and submitted the xerox copy of the same, which was received by PW.1 on 04.03.2003. On 04.03.2003, PW.1 sent a notice in Form-VI under Section 14A of the Act along with a letter to A3, asking him to furnish their license/ownership particulars by registered post. However, the said letter returned undelivered by the postal authorities with an endorsement 'not in 4 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 mill'. On 21.03.2003, PW.1 addressed a letter to the Assistant Food Controller, Zone-III, Headquarters Guntur, with a request to furnish the license particulars of the A3 Firm, but however, there was no response. Thereafter, on 01.04.2003, PW.1 made further efforts and addressed a letter along with Form-VI notice to A3 firm, which was also returned undelivered. Thereafter, on 17.06.2003, PW.1 submitted a detailed report to the State Food (Health) Authority through Gazetted Food Inspector & Local (Health) Authority, Nalgonda District, seeking necessary orders. On 15.07.2003, PW.1 addressed a letter to the Assistant Commercial Tax Officer, Macherla, Guntur District, requesting to furnish license particulars of A3 Firm. In response, the Food Inspector, Division-III, Guntur District, has furnished license and ownership particulars of A3, vide letter No.301/ZIII/2003, dated 23.07.2003, along with letter submitted by the A3. The Assistant Commercial Tax Officer, Macherla, Guntur District, also furnished the license/ownership particulars of A3 vide Lr.No.NRP/D-7/1/2729, dated 25.07.2003. PW.1 submitted the said particulars to the Director & Food (Health) Authority, Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad on 14.08.2003. The State Food (Health) Authority, Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad has accorded written consent under Section 20(1) of the Act for launching the prosecution against A1 to A3, vide order, dated 20.09.2003, for selling adulterated Redgram Dal for human consumption. As there was some mistake in 5 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 mentioning the name of A3, the Gazetted Food Inspector & Local (Health) Authority, Nalgonda District, vide letter, dated 08.10.2003, requested the State Food (Health) Authority, Andhra Pradesh, Hyderabad, to issue necessary corrigendum to the written consent orders, dated 20.09.2003. Accordingly, the State Food (Health) Authority, Andhra Pradesh, has issued corrigendum, dated 18.11.2003. Pursuant to the permission to launch prosecution, PW.1 filed the subject complaint before the trial Court on 18.12.2003 and issued notice under Section 13(2) of the Act to A1 to A3 on 24.12.2003. T. Suresh, vs State Of A.P., on 28 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156749863/ 2 6. The learned Magistrate took cognizance against A1 to A3 on 20.12.2003, for the offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Act for violation of provisions of Sections 7(i) and 2(ia)(i) of the Act. To prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution examined P.Ws.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.52. On behalf of the accused, no evidence, either oral or documentary, has been adduced. 7. Aggrieved by the same, A2 and A3 preferred both these Criminal Revision Cases. 8. The learned counsel for the petitioners/A2 and A3 would submit that both the Courts below erred in properly appreciating the evidence on record. PW.2, a panch witness, did not support the case of prosecution and his evidence is not corroborated with the evidence of PW.1. Taking this Court through the chronology of events, learned counsel for the petitioners/A2 and A3 submitted that the sample of the alleged adulterated Redgram Dal was lifted on 17.12.2002. Permission to launch prosecution against the accused was sanctioned on 20.09.2003. PW.1 filed the subject complaint before the Court below on 18.12.2003 and a notice under Section 13(2) of the Act was issued to the petitioners/A2 and A3 on 24.12.2003. Hence, there was inordinate delay in launching prosecution against the petitioners/A2 and A3, which deprived their valuable right under section 13(2) of the Act to seek permission to send the sample to the Central Food Laboratory for second analysis. Further, as per Section 11(4) of the Act, an article of food seized under Section 10(4) and any adulterant seized under Section 10(6) of the Act shall be produced before the Magistrate as soon as possible, not later than 7 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 seven days after the receipt of report of Public Analyst, which is patently absent in the instant case. Further, the very collection of sample was not in accordance with the relevant Rules and drawing of sample itself was wrong. The action against the petitioners/A2 and A3 stands vitiated on account of inordinate and deliberate delay in launching prosecution against them, thereby depriving them of the valuable rights conferred under the Act. Both the Courts below erroneously convicted the petitioners/A2 and A3 of the offence alleged against them. It is a fit case to extend benefit of doubt to the petitioners/A2 and A3 and acquit them of the offence alleged against them and ultimately prayed to allow the Criminal Revision Cases as prayed for. 9.
texts.arguments: On the other hand, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor supported the judgment impugned in these Criminal Revision Cases and contended that there are no circumstances to interfere with the impugned judgment. Here, it is apt to extract Section 11 (4) of the Act, which reads as follows: 11. Procedure to be followed by food inspectors -- (1) xxxx (2) xxxx (3) xxxx 10 Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Crl.R.C.Nos.576 & 580 of 2007 (4) An article of food seized under sub-section (4) of section 10, unless destroyed under subsection (4A) of that section, and any adulterant seized under sub-section (6) of that section shall be produced before a magistrate as soon as possible and in any case not later than seven days after the receipt of the report of the public analyst Provided that if an application is made to the magistrate in this behalf by the person from whom any article of food has been seized, the magistrate shall by order in writing direct the food inspector to produce such article before him within such time as may be specified in the order. 15. Further, Section 13(2) of the Act reads as follows: On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from whom the sample of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such person or persons that if it is so desired, either or T.
